capabilities.title: Local React application with loopback service and typed client
capabilities.contract: The renderer uses typed HTTP and Electron application-client operations, including supporting Proposal summaries, against local application services; credentials and privileged model operations remain server-side.
capabilities.persistence: No renderer access to secrets, files, or SQLite.

capabilities.title: Health reporting and recoverable client errors
capabilities.contract: Health and stable error codes, including streaming failures carried across the Electron bridge, allow the renderer to present recoverable failures without exposing secrets or full Article bodies.
capabilities.persistence: Errors are transient UI state; sensitive values are not included in the transport contract.

capabilities.title: Separate Editorial Workspace, Style Profile, and Application Settings screens
capabilities.contract: Application Settings and Style Profile are standalone application screens with a labeled back action. Style Profile opens from the Library, its shortcut, and Assistant result links, preserves the selected Article and Workspace View, and remains usable without an Article. Its sidebar selects Detected characteristics, Typography rules, Manual rules, and Writing samples; narrow screens use a section selector. Switching sections preserves unfinished forms and resets the single content pane's scroll position. Neither screen belongs to Article Revision history.
capabilities.persistence: Screen selection is renderer state; Application Settings persist through their dedicated service contracts.

capabilities.title: Non-blocking first-run quick start
capabilities.contract: A compact first-run dialog explains Article writing, advisory Assistant output, and model-key setup without blocking editing. It directs an Author without a usable connection to AI Settings and can be reopened from About Settings.
capabilities.persistence: Browser storage contains only the versioned skladno.quick-start.v1 completion marker; no Article, Settings, or credential data is stored.

capabilities.title: Single-user, local-first operation
capabilities.contract: Articles, Draft checkpoints, materials, style samples, model preferences, and completed Proposal summaries persist in local SQLite storage through focused domain-specific repositories wired at local-service startup; no aggregate repository facade is required.
capabilities.persistence: SQLite is the active data store; private author data is not delegated to a remote application database.

capabilities.title: Reviewed Author-focused release summaries
capabilities.contract: The two public commands release and release:preview generate missing notes, display the notes and security classification for explicit terminal approval, verify core and browser gates, then commit the approved record with version changes before tagging and atomically pushing. Cancelled drafts are reusable without another provider call; noninteractive runs require an explicitly reviewed record. Unrelated worktree changes and source or draft edits during verification block release. Release preparation selects published Warplyn ancestors as the comparison point, using the previous stable for a stable version and the previous stable or preview for a preview. The first release requires the explicit inherited v0.5.5 baseline. A release-time OpenAI request using OPENAI_COMMIT_GENERATION_KEY drafts concise Author-focused entries from bounded source and dependency-manifest diffs and commit evidence, grouping visible changes and excluding internal or reverted effects. Generated entries explicitly classify evidenced bug fixes, which render in a separate Bug fixes section after other Changes. Older entries without classification retain their existing rendering. Failed, refused, malformed, or incomplete responses save no new record. Drafts suggest a security flag with justification and commit evidence for actual vulnerability fixes affecting shipped Warplyn. Maintainers review the wording and classification before publication; manual preparation remains available through the same commands. A reviewed security flag adds the existing .security suffix to a preview version and tag, while the record version and filename remain unsuffixed. Stable security classification blocks release because the existing security tag format supports previews only. The commands' comparison mode includes uncommitted public source changes and exits without publication. Both platform workflows publish one deterministic body from the versioned reviewed record and reject tag/classification mismatches. Maintenance-only releases use an explicit accurate message. Stale records, invalid evidence, and mismatched existing releases block publication rather than inventing or overwriting details.
capabilities.persistence: Reviewed release-notes/<version>.json records pin the source and baseline commits in Git. Generation requests response storage disabled and never persists the API key. Comparison previews stay in local Git metadata. The GitHub Release body is the installed app's summary source; runtime update discovery adds no provider calls or Author data storage.

capabilities.title: Secured Electron desktop client for Windows
capabilities.contract: The unsigned Windows 11 x64 application runs the existing React application in one context-isolated, sandboxed Electron window without a native menu bar. Every former menu action is a configurable Key Binding: workspace actions run in the renderer, and editing, window, close, quit, and update actions cross only as allowlisted native command IDs. CI publishes stable tags as GitHub releases and preview tags as prereleases only when the tagged commit is contained in main; manual release dispatches must run from main. Each release includes the installer, RELEASES manifest, and full package. Its Squirrel installer creates Desktop and Start menu shortcuts. New installer builds and the Windows executable use punk.link as publisher metadata; this does not establish a signed publisher identity. The main process composes local application services and exposes only allowlisted typed IPC operations. GitHub release discovery is optional, requires the author's stored network permission, and runs at every startup and then daily while the application remains open; the author chooses stable-only or prerelease-inclusive discovery, while download and restart remain explicit. Restart and update requires a Draft checkpoint and verified SQLite snapshot before native Squirrel apply.
capabilities.persistence: The desktop client uses the existing user-local .warplyn SQLite data. Runtime settings retain the network-permission, automatic-check, and prerelease-channel preferences, staged version, prior version, and one recovery snapshot reference without Article content. Install, upgrade, reinstall, and uninstall do not delete or rewrite that directory.
limitations: Windows releases are unsigned; signing remains in https://github.com/punk-link/warplyn/issues/41.
Independent installation and uninstallation acceptance remains required before publication.

capabilities.title: Secured Electron desktop client for Debian-based distributions
capabilities.contract: The unsigned Debian x64 application runs the existing context-isolated, sandboxed Electron workspace and local services from one Debian package. Ubuntu 22.04 x64 is the release-validation baseline; compatible Debian-based distributions may install the same package. CI publishes only tags whose commit is contained in main, and manual release dispatches must run from main. It preserves Article, Draft, Revision, backup, credential, renderer-isolation, single-window, native-dialog, and shutdown guarantees. After author-approved GitHub access, About Settings can show the newest matching Debian release and open its release notes. Package-manager upgrades or manual .deb reinstalls remain author-controlled; Linux exposes no in-app download or apply action.
capabilities.persistence: Electron runtime state uses Linux userData while Article data remains in the resolved user-local .warplyn directory. Install, upgrade, reinstall, and uninstall do not delete or rewrite author data.
limitations: The installed Ubuntu 22.04 acceptance pass, including Secret Service, launcher, upgrade, reinstall, uninstall, and data-preservation evidence, remains required before any Linux target is guaranteed. Other compatible Debian-based distributions require the same pass; ARM64, RPM, Snap, Flatpak, AppImage, and in-app Linux updates require separate demand and acceptance evidence.

capabilities.title: Desktop-ready responsive shell
capabilities.contract: The desktop shell supports collapsed panels, responsive workspace layout, and a prominent non-blocking warning with a direct AI Settings action whenever no active connected AI connection is available.
capabilities.persistence: Workspace layout and proposal-advisory dismissal preferences are persisted locally in browser storage; AI connection readiness is read from application settings.
limitations: Mobile and browser-offline modes remain deferred.

scenarios.title: Release summaries use the reviewed reachable commit range
preconditions: Release history contains stable, preview, draft, legacy, and unrelated releases.
scenarios.event: A maintainer prepares and validates a release summary.
expected: The correct ancestor baseline and reachable commits are selected, entries cite in-range evidence, and maintenance-only wording requires an explicit decision. Security classification requires a reviewed flag, justification, in-range evidence supporting a visible entry, and a matching preview tag.
forbidden: Unreviewed or stale notes, unsupported claims without evidence, or internal commit subjects automatically becoming benefits.

scenarios.title: Platform publication reuses the same release summary
preconditions: Both platform workflows publish the same tagged release record.
scenarios.event: A platform creates or retries publication of the release.
expected: Both platforms use the exact rendered body, and matching releases survive creation races and retries.
forbidden: A workflow overwrites mismatched notes or uploads assets after a tag, body, or channel mismatch.

scenarios.title: Typed client translates service conflicts safely
preconditions: The local service responds with a Draft conflict.
scenarios.event: The renderer saves a Draft through HttpApplicationClient.
expected: The client throws the typed renderer-safe conflict error.
forbidden: Renderer access to server internals or credentials.

scenarios.title: Client-visible failures use stable error codes
preconditions: An Assistant request fails before or during streaming.
scenarios.event: The application client receives the service response.
expected: The client exposes a stable error code for recoverable UI handling.
forbidden: Raw provider details rendered as the user-facing failure.

scenarios.title: Opening Settings preserves the workspace context
preconditions: An Article is open in the Editorial Workspace.
scenarios.event: The author opens Application Settings.
expected: Application Settings is displayed without creating an empty Article workspace.
forbidden: Opening Settings alters Article Revision history.

scenarios.title: Local data survives reopening SQLite
preconditions: An Article, Draft checkpoint, material, setting, artifact, and citation exist.
scenarios.event: The SQLite database is closed and reopened.
expected: The persisted local data can be read after reopening.
forbidden: Requiring a remote application database.

scenarios.title: Electron window preserves the renderer trust boundary
preconditions: The Windows desktop client starts.
scenarios.event: The main process creates its application window and receives navigation requests.
expected: Context isolation and sandboxing are enabled, Node integration is disabled, and only HTTP or HTTPS links may open in the system browser.
A second launch restores and focuses the existing window.
forbidden: Renderer access to Node, SQLite, credentials, arbitrary IPC, or non-web external schemes.

scenarios.title: Electron close coordinates the active Draft checkpoint
preconditions: The author closes the desktop window while an Article is active.
scenarios.event: The main process requests the renderer's latest Draft checkpoint.
expected: The application closes after a successful checkpoint.
A failed checkpoint offers a return action and an explicit quit-without-latest-checkpoint action.
forbidden: Claiming that an unsuccessful checkpoint was saved.

scenarios.title: Debian package lifecycle preserves author data
preconditions: An installed Ubuntu 22.04 x64 or compatible Debian-based preview has a disposable .warplyn directory containing an Article, Draft, Revision, and Settings.
scenarios.event: The author launches, upgrades or reinstalls, then uninstalls the Debian package.
expected: The existing data reopens after upgrade or reinstall and remains on disk after uninstall.
The app exposes no in-app downloader or updater.
forbidden: Squirrel or autoUpdater calls on Linux, or installer lifecycle actions deleting or rewriting the .warplyn directory.

scenarios.title: Linux release discovery remains manual to install
preconditions: A packaged Debian release has a newer matching Debian package on GitHub and the author has allowed update network access.
scenarios.event: The Linux desktop coordinator checks release metadata.
expected: It offers the newest matching Debian release and release notes without starting a download.
forbidden: Squirrel or autoUpdater calls on Linux, an in-app Linux download, or a discovery request without author permission.

scenarios.title: Packaged Windows preview opens the existing application
preconditions: The unsigned Windows 11 x64 preview is installed with a disposable local data directory.
scenarios.event: The author launches Warplyn and completes the desktop acceptance journey.
expected: The existing React workspace opens and the typed Article, Settings, Assistant, editorial, and fact-check operations use local application services without an HTTP server.
Installation creates Desktop and Start menu shortcuts for Warplyn.
forbidden: A second React application or renderer access to privileged resources.

scenarios.title: Desktop reinstall and uninstall preserve local author data
preconditions: The disposable .warplyn directory contains an Article, Draft, Revision, and Settings.
scenarios.event: The preview is upgraded or reinstalled and then uninstalled.
expected: The existing data reopens after upgrade or reinstall and remains on disk after uninstall.
forbidden: Installer lifecycle actions deleting or rewriting the .warplyn directory.

scenarios.title: Update discovery is author-controlled
preconditions: A packaged Windows x64 release has a newer stable release or prerelease on GitHub and the author has allowed update network access.
scenarios.event: The desktop coordinator checks release metadata.
expected: Only the newest complete compatible release allowed by the stable-only or prerelease-inclusive preference is offered and no download starts before the author requests it.
forbidden: Making an update-discovery request without author permission or sending Article content or raw GitHub errors to the renderer.

scenarios.title: Restart and update retains recovery state
preconditions: A stable or preview update is staged.
scenarios.event: The author requests Restart and update.
expected: A Draft checkpoint and SQLite snapshot succeed before native apply.
forbidden: Applying an update after a failed checkpoint or snapshot.

scenarios.title: Desktop shell restores panel layout preferences
preconditions: Stored workspace layout settings are present.
scenarios.event: The Editorial Workspace loads.
expected: The desktop shell restores its panel layout and clears migrated legacy keys.
forbidden: A missing preference prevents the workspace from rendering.

scenarios.title: Missing AI connection is visible from the workspace
preconditions: No active connected AI connection is available.
scenarios.event: The author opens the Editorial Workspace or selects Add model key.
expected: A non-blocking Assistant warning explains that local writing remains available and AI-assisted actions need a configured model connection, including supported local models.
Add model key opens the AI Settings section.
The warning is absent while configuration loads or when an active connected connection is available.
forbidden: Preventing Article editing or showing the warning for a usable active connection.

scenarios.title: Quick start appears on first launch
preconditions: The local profile has no quick-start completion marker.
scenarios.event: The Author opens Warplyn.
expected: The quick start opens with accessible controls and focus.
An Author without a usable connection sees Add model key; an Author with one sees Start writing.
forbidden: Blocking Article editing or storing credentials or Article data in browser storage.

scenarios.title: Quick start dismissal is remembered
preconditions: The quick start is open.
scenarios.event: The Author skips, closes, or presses Escape.
expected: Only the versioned completion marker is stored.
Later launches do not reopen the dialog automatically.
forbidden: Changing an Article, Draft, Revision, or saved Settings.

scenarios.title: Quick start can be reopened from About Settings
preconditions: The Author has dismissed the quick start.
scenarios.event: The Author selects Quick start in About Settings.
expected: The dialog reopens without modifying the current Article or saved Settings.
forbidden: Resetting the completion marker or creating Article history.

scenarios.title: Quick start directs missing model-key setup to AI Settings
preconditions: No usable AI connection exists.
scenarios.event: The Author selects Add model key in the quick start.
expected: The dialog closes and AI Settings opens.
forbidden: Handling or displaying a credential in the tutorial.
